prompt: Filter a list without replacing it. Complete the removeShorterThan method so it removes every word shorter than minLen from the given ArrayList in place and returns that same list.
explanation: Removing while looping forward with an index is the classic ArrayList trap: when you remove element i, the next element slides into slot i and gets skipped. An Iterator's remove method (or removeIf, or a loop that walks backwards) removes safely. Because the method mutates and returns the list it was given, the tests can confirm with == that no new list was created.
hints: A forward index loop that calls words.remove(i) will skip the element after each removal -- try it mentally on [a, b, c].
Get an Iterator with words.iterator(); calling it.remove() right after it.next() deletes safely. words.removeIf(...) is the one-line shortcut.
Mutate the list you were handed and return that exact reference; do not construct a new ArrayList.
